sections.h2: Where the Lawrence County recorder's office is
sections.html:
The Lawrence County Recorder is inside the Court House at 111 South 4th Street, Suite 21, in Ironton, OH 45638. Call 740-533-4314, fax 740-533-4411 or write recorder@lawrencecountyohiorecorder.org. Weekday hours are 8 to 4.

The office is the county's permanent land file. Documents it handles every day include warranty and quit claim deeds, survivorship deeds, sheriff's deeds, certificates of transfer, affidavits of transfer, life estate terminations and transfer on death designation and confirmation affidavits. It also files mortgage releases and assignments, land contracts, plats, powers of attorney, zoning maps and a long run of liens, from mechanic's liens to federal tax liens and child support liens.

sections.h2: What it costs to record a deed
sections.html:
On January 1, 2025 most recording fees went up by $5.00, the preservation surcharge that Senate Bill 94 allowed. A one or two page document now runs $39.00 and every added page costs $8.00. Half of what the office collects is sent to the state for the Ohio Housing Trust Fund, consistent with section 317.32.

Lawrence County Recorder charges for a deed
ChargeAmount
One or two pages$39.00
Each added page$8.00
Ten pages in all$103.00
Reference to an earlier document$4.00 each
Deed that misses the layout rules$20.00 extra

The recorder's fee is only one piece of closing. The credits on second half 2025 tax bills are another, and the auditor posts those by school district.

Prepare the deed to the layout in section 317.114, which covers documents prepared after June 30, 2009. A deed that misses it costs $20.00 more. The office's checklist:

  • Computer-printed type, 10 point or larger.
  • Paper no smaller than 8.5 by 11 and no larger than 8.5 by 14 inches.
  • Black or blue ink, never highlighter.
  • A one inch margin down both sides and along the bottom of every page.
  • A 3 inch strip across the top of page one reserved for the recorder, auditor and engineer, then 1.5 inches on later pages.

Court and taxing authority papers, plats, DD214 discharges, state or federal documents and older instruments fall outside the rule. A margin guidelines PDF on the site helps whoever drafts the deed.

The auditor is at 111 S Fourth Street, phone (740) 533-4310, open weekdays 8 to 4. Section 319.202 sets the routine: the buyer files a statement of value, the seller pays the conveyance fee and the auditor endorses the deed.

The state charge in section 319.54(G)(3) is $1 or ten cents per $100, whichever is more, and a county can add a transfer tax capped at thirty cents per $100 under section 322.02. Totals differ by county, so the quickest check is the Conveyance Fee Calculator in the Tools menu of the auditor's site, which includes the parcel transfer fee. Type in a parcel count and a sale price, and it returns a charge.

The current index runs from 1982 for deeds, 1988 for mortgages, 1989 for financing statements and 1981 for leases, liens and miscellaneous records. A second online index reaches much further back.

  • Deed grantor and grantee entries date from 1818 to 1984, and mortgages from 1834 to 1988.
  • Plats are listed from 1818 to 2010, and leases from 1864 to 1981.
  • Index books online include deed volumes 1 through 475 and mortgage volumes 82 through 441.

Staff can help you search during business hours. Older easements can hide before 1982, so ask where the older books begin for your parcel if a title search stops at the current deed index.

Lawrence County had 55,710 people in mid 2025, which is 4.3 percent fewer than in April 2020, and 26,564 housing units. Owners occupy 72.3 percent of homes. The typical owned home was valued at $144,000 in 2020 to 2024, median gross rent is $848 and median household income is $58,325. Builders took out 23 permits in 2025, so new construction is scarce and resale homes make up most of the market.

sections.h2: House Bill 186 and your tax bill
sections.html:
An Inflation Cap Credit appears on second half 2025 real estate bills. It is based on new revenue each school district gained from the 20 mill floor measured against inflation, and it did not alter any appraised value. A buyer or title agent can view the credit by searching the parcel on the auditor's site.

An owner who paid before the credit was applied needs to do nothing, because any overpayment rolls into the 2026 first half bill. Ask the auditor how a carried credit should show on a closing statement.

Beyond the calculator, the Tools menu holds a Tax Estimator, a Sales Report, a Sales List and a Delinquency Report. The sales reports list recent sales in the county, which helps when you set a price. The site also carries a GIS parcel viewer through its map link, and a search page that shows the appraisal and payment history for any parcel.

Have the deed drafted to the layout rules and signed. Take it to the auditor, who collects the conveyance fee and endorses it, then to the recorder in Suite 21, which charges by page count. Before you do, run the calculator so the check is the right size. Mortgage releases and any older liens are recorded by the same office, so ask your title company to confirm each one was filed. Keep the endorsed deed and the receipt together for your closing file.

If your deed carries any reference to an earlier recorded document, count it before you leave home, since each reference adds $4.00 to the bill. Call the recorder at 740-533-4314 if you are unsure how many pages your signed deed runs, because the page count sets the fee. If the paper misses the margin rules the office still records it, but you pay the extra $20.00, so a quick check of type size and ink color saves money. Ironton sellers can also use the sales report on the auditor's site to see what nearby homes brought before settling on an asking price.

faqs.q: Where do I record a deed in Lawrence County, Ohio?
faqs.a: At the Lawrence County Recorder, Court House, 111 South 4th Street, Suite 21, Ironton, OH 45638, phone 740-533-4314. Stop at the county auditor first so the statement of value and conveyance fee are handled.

faqs.q: How much does the Lawrence County recorder charge for a deed?
faqs.a: $39.00 for one or two pages and $8.00 for each page after that, effective January 1, 2025. $4.00 reference fees and the $20.00 standardization charge apply when triggered.

faqs.q: Is there a way to estimate the Lawrence County conveyance fee?
faqs.a: The auditor's website has a Conveyance Fee Calculator, with parcel count and sale price as inputs, and it includes the parcel transfer fee. The auditor's office at (740) 533-4310 can confirm a figure.

faqs.q: What happens if my deed breaks the Ohio margin rules?
faqs.a: The recorder accepts it and adds $20.00. The 3 inch top margin on page one is reserved for the recorder, auditor and engineer. Court papers, plats, DD214s, state or federal documents and older instruments are exempt from the rule.

faqs.q: How far back do Lawrence County deed records run online?
faqs.a: The current index lists deeds from 1982 forward, and the older online index lists grantor and grantee entries from 1818 to 1984. Index books include deed volumes 1 through 475. Ask the recorder about anything the online index does not reach.
